I have what I need. Let me verify the material terms against the rule before submitting.

**Assessment of paragraph 4(a)/(b) (p0016):**

| Rule term | Document | Fallback test |
|---|---|---|
| Customer convenience right | Either Party may terminate for any reason after the Initial Term, 90 days' notice | 60–90 days' notice ✓ |
| Term length | 1-year Initial Term, 1-year auto-renewals | Not a multi-year lock-in; rolling 90-day exit after year one ✓ |
| Early-termination fee | None; Kubient keeps only fees *generated during* the 90-day notice period while still serving | ≤ 3 months' fees ✓ |
| Vendor convenience right | Only after the Initial Term, on 90 days' notice | Not fewer than 90 days ✓ (not walk-away) |
| Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees | N/A — revenue-share model (§5), no prepayment | Minor/inapplicable |

The Initial Term is exactly 12 months, so the "no convenience right in a term longer than 12 months" trigger is not met, and the mid-term bar is symmetric — it equally prevents Kubient from walking away on us.

input.quote: Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party. Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement,
input.rationale: The clause sits at the playbook fallback and is therefore acceptable without redline. (1) Customer convenience right: after the one-year Initial Term, AP may terminate "for any reason" on ninety (90) days' written notice, which is at the outer edge of the fallback's 60–90 day range and, given the 1-year auto-renewal cycle, gives AP a rolling exit rather than a multi-year lock-in. (2) Term length: the Initial Term is exactly one (1) year, so the detection trigger for "absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months" is not met; the mid-term bar is also symmetric and equally prevents Kubient from walking away on us mid-term, so it partly benefits AP. (3) Vendor convenience right: Kubient may terminate at will only following the Initial Term and only on ninety (90) days' notice — not fewer than 90 days, so it does not fall into walk-away territory. (4) No early-termination fee or penalty is imposed; Kubient is entitled only to fees "generated during the termination period," i.e. revenue actually earned across the 90-day notice period while it continues to provide the Services, which is within the fallback's 3-months'-fees cap rather than a penalty. Noted but not flagged as deviations (minor sub-elements short of preferred): the notice period is 90 days rather than the preferred 30 days; Kubient's convenience right runs at any time after the Initial Term rather than only at the end of a renewal term; and there is no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees — the latter is inapplicable because §5 (p0023) establishes a revenue-share model with payment flowing from Kubient to AP within 7 days of receipt, so AP prepays no fees that could require refund.
